hints.title: Exact Window Average Obstacle
hints.text: Summing every subarray of length k from scratch takes quadratic time. How can you compare the sum directly to k * threshold and update in O(1) time per shift?

hints.title: Threshold Target Invariant
hints.text: The average condition sum // k >= threshold is equivalent to sum >= k * threshold, avoiding floating-point division.

hints.title: Fixed Window Accumulation Procedure
hints.text: Let target = k * threshold. Compute window sum of first k elements. If window >= target, count = 1, else 0. Slide right from index k to n - 1: add arr[i] and subtract arr[i - k]. If window >= target, increment count. Return count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: k: subarray window size (1 <= k <= N)
complexity.notes: Single pass fixed-size sliding window with O(1) delta sum updates and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Computing sum of each size-k window independently takes O(N * k) which takes 10^10 operations for large k.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Multiplying threshold by k to avoid division and maintaining rolling sum.
